comment: THE CAPABILITY x PROTOCOL EQUALITY MATRIX -- the equality doctrine, as a pinned instrument.
Owner's ruling (repeated; this file exists so it never has to be repeated again):
'breakers, hooks, auditing -- list all the core functionality. outside should ONLY BE
Auth, Store, Protocols, i.e. Plugins. Any plugin gets all functionality.
LLM == MCP == A2A -- just different protocols not different pathway through engine at all.'
Every CORE CAPABILITY x PROTOCOL PLANE cell is exactly one of:
proven          -- with `test`: `<repo-relative test file>::<test fn>`. The gate
(crates/busbar/tests/capability_equality.rs) verifies the file exists and
the fn is in it, so a proven cell cannot outlive its evidence.
missing         -- the capability does not reach this plane today, or no test proves it does.
A proof that nobody watched is a claim; MISSING is the honest state until
a named test exists. The missing set is the work queue, and every umbrella
run prints it (scripts/capability-equality-summary.py, wired into
scripts/full-gate.sh) -- green stays green, but the gap is NAMED.
not-applicable  -- with `reason`: a one-line argument. N/A is a claim, not an escape; the
gate refuses an n/a cell whose argument is missing or trivial.
The capability list is the one-of-each modules in core -- each a mechanism that exists
exactly once and that every plane is owed:
breaker.rs, failover/, hooks/, audit/, governance/, metrics.rs, trust/, net_guard.rs,
egress_auth/, catalogue.rs, and the disposition pipeline (proto/ Stage 1 -> breaker::classify).
CHANGING THIS FILE: close a cell by flipping it to `proven` WITH the test that proves it, in
the SAME commit as the test. Regressing a proven cell (its test vanishes or is renamed) is RED.
Adding a capability or plane without filling its whole row/column is RED (the cross product is
exact). Do not delete a capability to shrink the queue.

capabilities.breaker-trip: a failing upstream target records into the ONE core breaker cell (LaneRuntime, (pool,lane)-keyed) and the cell opens
capabilities.breaker-fastfail: a tripped target is refused before dispatch in milliseconds, not after the full timeout, via try_admit_breaker
capabilities.failover-reroute: a second interchangeable candidate is tried before the first byte, through ONE selection loop on every plane: failover::walk_with. It owns the whole decision -- is there a candidate set, is this hop a repeat and is that allowed, do the candidates' pins agree, will the breaker admit, and what the refusal is. A plane supplies exactly two values and no loop: the ORDER (which candidate is asked next) and the ADMISSION. MCP and A2A reach it via failover::walk (operator members: order, LaneRuntime::try_admit_breaker); the model plane reaches it via proxy::select::pick_among (SWRR / routing-policy / session-affinity order, LaneRuntime::try_admit -- the SAME breaker FSM, cell and single-flight probe, plus that plane's concurrency permit). The model plane's on_exhausted machinery (503 / fallback_pool / least_bad / queue, proxy/engine/walk.rs) is NOT selection: it is what that plane does after the one loop finds nothing, and it dispatches only through the loop's admission or its own documented least-bad breaker bypass
capabilities.hooks-tap: observe/transform hooks (rewrite, usage projection) run over the plane's payloads
capabilities.hooks-gate: hooks::gate::decide can refuse the plane's traffic before dispatch
capabilities.audit-chain: the plane's dispatches and refusals land in a tamper-evident hash chain (crate::audit)
capabilities.governance-budget: spend on the plane is attributed to the presenting key and budget limits refuse with a Retry-After
capabilities.disposition: the plane's upstream answers are normalized (Stage 1) and classified into Disposition (Stage 2, breaker::classify)
capabilities.metrics: the plane's traffic appears on the real /metrics scrape under its own plane label
capabilities.trust-pinning: the peer's artifact (schema digest / card fingerprint / SPKI) is pinned; drift is detected, demoted and refused
capabilities.net-guard: every outbound destination this role derives is SSRF-guarded through core net_guard (judged-address pinning, metadata refusal)
capabilities.egress-auth: outbound credentials are planned and injected by the one egress mechanism -- never a caller token passed through
capabilities.catalogue: what this caller may SEE is answered by the one core catalogue walk (catalogue::entitled), trust-gated per item

planes.llm: model traffic: app -> busbar -> provider, HTTP incl. SSE/binary streams (one plane, both halves)
planes.mcp-client: busbar's outbound leg to registered MCP servers -- streamable-HTTP and stdio; where the transport changes the answer, the cell's note says so
planes.mcp-server: busbar's MCP front door: inbound methods from clients and agents
planes.a2a-client: busbar issuing A2A requests: the relay leg to backend agents (JsonRpc, HttpJson, Grpc -- one relay below the transport axis), originate, card fetch
planes.a2a-server: busbar's A2A front door: inbound tasks/messages, plus this role's own outbound webhook push delivery
planes.voice-client: busbar's outbound duplex leg: the dialed WSS to the realtime voice provider (OpenAI Realtime / Gemini Live) and the telephony media egress (Twilio g711); one session is pinned to one provider socket for its whole lifetime
planes.voice-server: busbar's voice front door: inbound session-open ingress -- the browser sideband WebSocket and the telephony (Twilio) media-stream webhook -- that opens a governed duplex session

cells.reason: the front door is inbound; there is no upstream target whose availability could be recorded. A peer-initiated sampling/createMessage rides the LLM engine and is the llm cell's evidence.
inbound role; no upstream availability to record. The anomaly breaker (a2a/anomaly.rs) is behaviour trust, not availability, and must not be conflated with the core breaker.
the front door is inbound; admission-before-dispatch has no upstream target on this role. The outbound legs it triggers are the llm and mcp-client cells.
inbound role; there is no dispatch admission against an upstream to make fast. Refusing inbound work is the governance and trust cells' subject, not the breaker's.
inbound role; there is no candidate set to walk. Failover for work this role triggers belongs to the outbound cells (llm, mcp-client).
inbound role; there is no candidate set to walk on the receiving side. The relay's candidate walk is the a2a-client cell.

cells.note: the `prompt: rw` transform pass at mcp/method.rs (through the EngineHost::transform_over host seam, mirroring the LLM apply_global_rewrites) rewrites the tool-call arguments over the SAME InvokeReq projection the gate builds, BEFORE the upstream credential is leased. One wiring at the method layer covers both directions (no ungated production entry to the client leg), exactly as the hooks-gate cells.

same transform_over wiring at mcp/method.rs; the test asserts on the arguments the real upstream peer received (peer.last_mcp()). BYTE-IDENTICAL when no rewrite hook is attached (tap_attached misses).

the `prompt: rw` transform pass at a2a/receive.rs::admitted rewrites the submission params over the same InvokeReq projection the gate builds; the relay (a2a-client) leg runs downstream of that admission, so one wiring covers both directions. The test asserts on the params the backend actually received (h.sent()).
same transform_over wiring at a2a/receive.rs; BYTE-IDENTICAL verbatim passthrough when no rewrite hook is attached (the relay re-serializes the envelope only when a rewrite actually committed).
the gate sits at the method layer (mcp/method.rs) BEFORE the upstream leg; there is no ungated production entry to the client leg, so one battery covers both directions.

cells.reason: busbar-originated A2A traffic is not a second gate point: originate (mirror_push_config, refresh_listed_tasks) is called only from receive.rs::admitted, downstream of the proven inbound hooks gate, and push delivery targets the caller's own webhook, which the agent-submission gate has no semantic target for. Same rationale the mcp-client cell is proven under.

cells.note: closed by proxy/reqlog.rs -- a RECORD TYPE and nothing else, appended at the plane's one terminal (ingress::finish_inner) through the ONE mechanism in crate::audit. Scoped per principal like the MCP call log. The test drives a real request through build_router over a real socket and reads the chain back; deleting the append fails it and leaves the other 4,540 tests green. HONEST LIMIT: busbar_api::Store carries no model-request method, so this stream is a bounded in-memory window and a restart loses it -- adding durability is a plugin-ABI change fanned out to four store repos and is deliberately not made here. Nothing may call it durable until that method exists.

the outcome of the leg BUSBAR issues is what the chain carries: a leg that went out and came back badly is chained as `dispatched` + `upstream_failed`, a leg that worked as `dispatched` with an empty reason. Both are driven through one principal, one server and one tool differing only in the upstream's answer, so the pin cannot be satisfied by a constant. Watched red: deleting the reason token at method.rs's Outcome::UpstreamFailed arm fails it and leaves the two front-door tests green.

the hop busbar ISSUES is chained: `task.delegated` naming who delegated and to which registered agent, appended BEFORE the socket, in the same per-task chain as the submission and verified by crate::audit::verify_chain. A failed hop is chained too and ends terminally (a_failed_hop_is_chained_too_and_the_chain_carries_its_terminal_outcome). Watched red: removing the record_dispatch call in a2a/receive.rs fails both. STILL OPEN on this plane's sibling: push-notification DELIVERY (a2a/pushdeliver.rs) chains nothing -- that is the a2a-server role's own outbound leg, tracked in the gap report, not claimed here.

RE-POINTED. The previous pin (provenance_tests::an_untouched_chain_verifies_and_its_links_are_actual_links) builds a synthetic TaskChain in-process and would have passed unchanged if the front door chained nothing at all -- a cell green on evidence that never touches the plane. The new pin POSTs message/send at a real listener through build_router and reads the events back out of an attached store, so an empty read-back is a failure rather than a pass. This plane's own outbound webhook delivery is covered by the three task.push_* tests in pushdeliver_tests.rs, added with it: before them a delivery refused by the delivery-time SSRF guard left no record anywhere.

the per-upstream sampling budget, charged BEFORE the model leg in mcp::sampling::satisfy_upstream_ask when busbar itself originates the completion. Red-proven by deleting the try_spend call from the production path: this test failed and the other five sampling_satisfy tests plus all three sampling_spend unit tests stayed green.

cells.reason: disposition classifies an upstream's ANSWER; the inbound role has no upstream answer to classify. Rendering a refusal to a caller is the response path, not disposition.
disposition classifies an upstream's ANSWER; the inbound role has no upstream answer to classify. Rendering a refusal to a caller is the response path, not disposition.

cells.note: despite its name the test drives all three planes and asserts the llm, mcp and a2a series labels on one real scrape.

the MODEL PLANE'S OWN client-leg families -- busbar_upstream_attempts_total / busbar_upstream_failures_total, same label keys, same disposition vocabulary -- emitted from the one counted wire seam (mcp::client::wire::send), so the plane label is no longer front-door-only. Its twin an_upstream_that_cannot_be_reached_is_counted_as_a_transient_failure_beside_its_attempt covers the failure half.

the same two client-leg families, emitted from a2a::relay::prepare and count_leg_failure, labelled with the operator's agent_def id and the binding word off the closed transport axis. Its twin a_backend_that_cannot_be_reached_is_counted_as_a_transient_upstream_failure covers the failure half.

cells.reason: LLM providers are operator-declared config endpoints, not peer-published artifacts; there is no upstream-authored schema or card to pin. The trust lifecycle governs artifacts a peer authors.

LLM egress targets are operator-configured provider endpoints; no request-authored URL reaches the LLM egress path, so there is no SSRF surface -- which is why grep finds no net_guard consumer under proxy/.
the inbound listener derives no outbound destination of its own; the destinations its work triggers are guarded in the mcp-client and llm cells.

cells.note: this role's own outbound is webhook push delivery, and it is guarded -- the PUSH-DELIVER TCK waivers exist because this guard correctly wins over the conformance score.

cells.reason: this role's only outbound (peer sampling) rides the LLM engine, whose credential injection is the llm cell; inbound caller authentication is the Auth plugin's subject, not egress.

the voice front door is an inbound role; opening a session records no upstream target availability, so there is no core breaker cell to trip here -- the outbound provider dial a session triggers is the voice-client cell's subject, the same shape mcp-server/a2a-server breaker-trip are N/A under.

the inbound session-open has no dispatch against an upstream to make fast; admission-before-dial against a tripped provider cell belongs to the voice-client dial leg, not the front door that merely accepts the session.

a duplex voice session is pinned to one provider socket for its whole lifetime, so there is no pre-first-byte candidate set to walk on the dial leg; a dropped session re-dials as a NEW session, never a mid-session reroute, so failover::walk has nothing to select over here.

the front door is an inbound role with no candidate set to walk; failover selection over interchangeable provider members is the outbound voice-client leg's decision, exactly as a2a-server reroute is not-applicable on the receiving side.

disposition classifies a discrete upstream ANSWER (proto Stage 1 -> breaker::classify); a duplex frame stream has no per-hop answer to normalize -- a fatal provider frame closes the session rather than resolving into a Disposition, so Stage 2 has nothing to classify on the dial leg.

disposition classifies an upstream's ANSWER; the inbound session-open has no upstream answer to normalize, so Stage-1/Stage-2 classification has no subject here -- the same argument mcp-server and a2a-server disposition are not-applicable under.

voice providers (OpenAI Realtime, Gemini Live) are operator-declared config endpoints, not peer-published artifacts; there is no upstream-authored schema digest or card to pin -- exactly the argument the llm dial cell is not-applicable under.

the browser-sideband and telephony callers that reach the front door publish no artifact (no schema digest, agent card, or SPKI) for the trust lifecycle to pin; there is no peer-authored object whose drift could be detected, unlike the a2a-server card-fingerprint cell.

the provider WSS is an operator-configured endpoint and no request-authored URL reaches the dial, so there is no SSRF surface on the outbound leg (the net_guard resolve->pin->guard at topology::dial_provider is defense-in-depth, not a request-URL guard); revisit if a T3 request-authored callback URL is ever dialed, like a2a-server push delivery.

the inbound session listener derives no outbound destination of its own; the one outbound a session triggers is the provider dial, guarded (defense-in-depth) on the voice-client leg, so the front door has no request-authored egress to SSRF-guard.

the front door's only outbound is the provider dial, whose credential injection is the voice-client egress-auth cell; the inbound caller's own bearer is authenticated by the Auth plugin, which is not egress credential planning -- the same split mcp-server egress-auth is not-applicable under.

the voice plane's config is the SINGULAR streams: section, not a named-definition map like tools:/agents:, so there are no per-item registrations for catalogue::entitled to walk and trust-gate; named_def_list and registry_contains are None by construction, so no caller-visible catalogue exists on this plane.

the voice plane declares the SINGULAR streams: section, not a named-definition map, so the front door exposes no per-item registry for catalogue::entitled to walk; named_def_list/registry_contains are None, so there is no caller-visible catalogue surface to trust-gate.
